_about: Hindcast vocabulary: the may / may-not list of docs/hindcast/DESIGN.md section 3 as data (backlog H-205).
hindcast/lint.py enforces it on every candidate card, proposal and GitHub issue body; the skill's
references/vocabulary.md is generated from this file (python -m hindcast.lint --markdown).
honesty_statement: the paragraph that appears verbatim on every page, card and proposal. lint.py removes it from a
text before checking, so its own wording ('what glucose would have done') never trips a rule.
may: phrases every surface may use; tests assert each one passes every kind.
may_not: refused wording. `pattern` is a case-insensitive regex; when absent the phrase is matched as whole words.
`example` is a sentence the tests expect to be refused, `why` the reason shown to the author.
privacy: regexes applied to kind 'issue' only. The repository is public: what ns_settings.json already publishes
(preference names and values) may appear in an issue; what Nightscout holds (glucose values, insulin units per day,
loop counts per day, transcript excerpts, prediction arrays) may not. `passes` lists wording the rule must accept.
honesty_statement: Hindcast replays the loop's decisions under other settings over the glucose and insulin history that the phone's own settings produced. It says where and how much the loop would have asked differently; it cannot say what glucose would have done. A variant that boluses earlier is charged for its bolus and for the later ones the phone actually gave, so deltas overstate aggressive settings and understate gentle ones. The base replay disagrees with the phone in about 4 % of loops; differences smaller than that floor are ties. Nothing here changes the phone; settings are for you and your care team to review. This is one person's insulin dosing, not medical advice.

may_not.why: an outcome judgement; the replay only knows what the loop would have asked, not what followed
may_not.example: This variant is better on the sport day.

may_not.why: an outcome judgement; the table is in review order, not a ranking by outcome
an outcome judgement; nothing here is optimised for glucose
a safety judgement about glucose outcomes; the replay cannot make one ('safety reading' for a number a human checks is fine)
a glucose outcome; virtual glucose is never computed
a glucose outcome; virtual glucose is never computed
may_not.example: This gives fewer highs after breakfast.

may_not.why: a glucose outcome; the replay has no glucose response model
may_not.example: The result is tighter control in the morning.

may_not.why: a time-in-range figure is an outcome statistic that cannot follow from a decision replay
counting lows or highs is a glucose outcome; a recorded low may only be named positionally ('a low followed here')
may_not.example: The hypo count drops from 3 to 1.

may_not.why: a counterfactual glucose outcome; the replay cannot say what glucose would have done
may_not.example: It would have prevented the low at 09:41.

may_not.why: a hindcast says nothing about the future; it re-runs recorded days
may_not.example: This setting will reduce the morning rise.

may_not.why: settings are recommended for review by the person and their care team, never as such
a counterfactual glucose statement; the replay only knows the loop's decisions
may_not.example: Glucose would have stayed under 10 after lunch.
The variant leads to lower glucose in the afternoon.

may_not.why: a value judgement about outcomes; say what the loop would have asked instead

may_not.example: The weekend looks worse with this cap.

privacy.name: U/day
privacy.why: insulin per day (and a share of the total daily dose) is Nightscout data; it belongs in the private artifact, not in a public issue
privacy.example: SMB total +4.05 U/day on the first day.
privacy.passes: the day count and the parameter ranges are in the campaign table

privacy.name: mmol
privacy.why: a glucose value or unit; glucose data never leaves the private artifact

privacy.name: mg/dl
privacy.example: BG 65 mg/dl at the time of the loop.
privacy.passes: smb_delivery_ratio_bg_range stays at its current value

privacy.name: BG-like number next to a time
privacy.why: a glucose reading with its time stamp is a transcript excerpt (2.0-25.9 read as mmol, 40-399 as mg/dl; a number followed by trials/variants/days/% is a count and passes)
privacy.example: At 09:00 the reading was 5.4 and falling.
privacy.passes: 19:42 round 4, 240 trials done; the 2026-09-06T09:00:37Z loop differs, see the artifact

privacy.name: Microbolusing
privacy.why: wording of the loop's reason or consoleError text is a transcript excerpt
privacy.passes: the variant would have microbolused in more loops than base

privacy.name: predBGs
privacy.why: prediction arrays are Nightscout devicestatus data
privacy.passes: both prediction fans are in the drill-down of the artifact

privacy.name: insulin units
privacy.why: an insulin amount in units is dosing data, however small; say the direction and the floor multiple ('asked for less insulin in rising loops, 2.9 x the floor') and leave the amount to the private artifact (only a fixed tolerance under 0.1 U after 'within', such as 'SMB within 0.05 U', passes)
privacy.example: would have asked for 0.06 U less than base in the other loops
privacy.passes: would have asked for less insulin than base in rising loops (2.9 x the floor) over 1 day; SMB within 0.05 U; UAM and enable_UAM may be named

privacy.name: loop count
privacy.why: loop counts describe the person's data volume; issues carry day counts, trial counts and decision shares (% of loops) only
privacy.passes: replayed over 7 days, 240 trials done; the 09:00 loop differs; cap binding 9.7 % of loops

privacy.name: carbs
privacy.why: carb entries are Nightscout treatment data
privacy.passes: carbs are shown as triangles on the artifact

privacy.name: glucose statistic
privacy.why: a share of time above or below a glucose level is Nightscout-derived data
privacy.passes: cap binding 9.7 % of loops (a decision share, no glucose level)
